facts.fact: FAO says the EOSTAT-Zimbabwe project, launched in 2023 with African Development Bank funding and implemented with the Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development, ZIMSTAT, ZINGSA and others, is rolling out an Earth-observation crop monitoring system and crop type and yield data practices.

systems.owner: FAO with the Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development

facts.fact: Digital Earth Africa and SASSCAL agreed to build the AgriWatch dashboard on DE Africa Earth-observation products for crop-cycle, rangeland and rainfall monitoring, with AgriWatch covering this country among the six SASSCAL states.

note: Private agritech and insurance platform with no government or research-institute part stated.

facts.fact: FAO says EOSTAT Phase II, launched with the Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development, will make satellite crop type mapping routine and expand Earth-observation tools for drought and flood early warning, after a first phase that produced a 2023 winter wheat map, a 2023/24 summer crop type map and pilot drought and flood tools.

systems.platform: Earth observation time series and anomaly detection
systems.owner: FAO with ZIMSTAT, ZINGSA, SIRDC, ZCHPC and the Meteorological Services Department

facts.fact: FAO says its EOSTAT system helps Zimbabwe generate crop and yield estimates from satellite data with over 80 percent accuracy and tracks droughts and floods in real time, and a Ministry early warning specialist describes it as modernising agricultural monitoring.

systems.owner: FAO with the Ministry of Agriculture; Zimbabwe Space Agency and NUST trained

facts.fact: EO Handbook 2026 reports that by 2025 Zimbabwean technicians at ZCHPC operated Sen4Stat to produce national crop type maps and maize acreage estimates for the agriculture ministry and ZIMSTAT, and a field-level drought monitoring tool was automated in 2025.
facts.system: Sen4Stat / national EO-assisted crop monitoring system

facts.fact: NASA Harvest reports that CIMMYT's April 2025 field campaign collected 4,600 georeferenced crop samples in Zimbabwe, combined within ESA's WorldCereal system, and Zimbabwean agency participants attended the November 2025 Zambia workshop.

The Herald reports that the Farmer's Basket hybrid index insurance pilot of 2024, run by the Insurance and Pensions Commission with government ministries, IFC and WFP, bases its weather index on daily satellite data.
The Herald reports that 1,800 smallholder farmers received US$65 payouts each in the Farmer's Basket pilot, whose weather index uses daily satellite data.

systems.owner: Insurance and Pensions Commission with Insurance Council, IFC, WFP and ministries

facts.fact: FEWS NET's October 2026 Southern Africa seasonal monitor reports well-above-average NDVI vegetation and above-average soil moisture in southern Zimbabwe.
